content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The Agreement contains no exclusivity obligation binding us. Section 1 affirmatively cuts the other way:

> "Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties."

That is an express non-exclusivity disclaimer plus a preserved right to use other agents and sell to third parties — squarely at the playbook's **preferred** position, better than the fallback (category/12-month-limited exclusivity with a performance exit).

The remaining "exclusive" hits are unrelated and none restrict our sourcing freedom:
- **p0002** — license to us is *non-exclusive* (a limitation on the license grant, not on our purchasing).
- **p0064** — exclusive jurisdiction/venue (New York) — dispute resolution, not dealing.
- **p0065** — each party's marks are its exclusive property.
- **p0072** — entire-agreement ("completely and exclusively states the agreement").
- **p0073** — sole and exclusive benefit of the parties (no third-party beneficiaries).

Targeted searches for the classic detection phrasing ("sole supplier / sole source", "all of its requirements from", "shall not engage", third-party procurement restrictions) returned nothing binding on us. No deviation, and nothing to narrow.
